sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface HA immunostaining confirmed (PMC8119971, L5/L6); steady-state surface expression detected though typically weaker than α2δ-1-HA; surface level not reduced by dominant-negative Rab11a(S25N), indicating intact surface trafficking via a Rab11a-independent route (L7). No direct voltage-gated calcium channel current measurement reported for this tagged construct.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names the junction as between aa 36 and 37 of mouse CACNA2D3; mouse and human CACNA2D3 share a 28 aa signal peptide (UniProt Q8VHN6 vs Q8IZS9), so mouse aa 36 maps directly to human aa 36. Python confirms residue 36 = Q and residue 37 = I in the canonical human sequence, both within the extracellular span (29–1091). The site is 8 residues into the mature ectodomain, well clear of the signal-peptide cleavage site and any TM boundary. L2, L5, L6, and L7 all independently confirm that this HA-tagged α2δ-3 construct reaches the cell surface. Full-length mouse CACNA2D3 with a double HA-tag inserted between aa 36 and 37, expressed in a heterologous system; the same construct (α2δ-3-HA, ref 14) is used in PMC8119971 for cell-surface immunostaining and trafficking experiments.

sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell immunolabeling of the HA epitope confirmed surface display of the full-length membrane-anchored α2δ-3 construct (L4). No channel current or other functional assay reported for this specific construct.
sites.rationale: L3 states the tag is placed 'right after the signal sequence' in their independently cloned mouse CACNA2D3 constructs; no residue number is given, so the position is topology-derived. The canonical signal peptide of both mouse and human CACNA2D3 ends at residue 28 (G), making insert_after_residue = 28 the unique junction consistent with 'right after the signal sequence'. Python confirms residue 28 = G and residue 29 = D (the mature N-terminus). This is a distinct construct from L1 (different GenBank accessions, different paper, different description). L4 confirms the tag is accessible on the extracellular surface by live-cell labeling. PMC8040823 (L3/L4) engineered a double HA-tag into the N-termini of all three α2δ subunits cloned from mouse brain cDNA (GenBank MK327276/MK327277/MK327280) 'right after the signal sequence'; live-cell surface immunolabeling of the HA epitope was used to compare isoform surface expression.

sources.claim: To this end a double HA-tag was engineered into N termini of all three α 2 δ subunits cloned from mouse brain complementary DNA (GenBank accession numbers MK327276 , MK327277 , and MK327280 ) right after the signal sequence.
